label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: All ten views in sides.png show a plain rectangular block, 24 by 24 by 40, square in plan. It reads as a pillar, not a console. There is no slanted control desk and no raised screen housing, and no dials or switches break the outline. The front, left, back and right views are the same rectangle, so the outline the brief describes is missing from every view.

M2.reason: The measured height is 40, which matches the 40 asked for (sizeOff 0). That is within 15% and fits 'waist high'. The brief gives no length or width.

M3.reason: None of the parts the brief names are there. There are no dials, no two screens and no row of switches. Every face in sides.png is flat and unbroken, including the top and the front.

M4.reason: The whole model wears one mottled grey texture that looks like concrete. There is no painted-metal casing and no glass or lit screens, and the dials and switches have no colours of their own. The regions a console would have are all missing, so they cannot carry the right colour or material.

M5.reason: There are no panel lines, dial faces, screen glow, switch markings, hazard paint or wear on any face. The only marks are the grain of the grey texture. The brief's worn industrial details are all missing.

M6.reason: In lineup.png, model A is a bare grey box next to a textured rock (C), a test sphere (B) and a leg bone (D). No player would take it for one of Half-Life's props or recognise it as a control console. It is plainly a placeholder.

M7.reason: It stands upright on its base, as the front-left and front-right views show. But all four sides are the same, so it has no front where the screens and controls face. The facing a console needs can't be checked and isn't there.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors (checkErrors empty). Its 12 triangles are well under twice the median of 62. It is a closed box with nothing open, inside out or floating.
